title: Mystery House
paragraphs: A mystery and suspense anthology represented by surviving standalone dramas. Where the historical record is incomplete, Golden Radio Hour keeps the uncertainty rather than assigning unsupported dates or episode order.

Mystery and suspense anthology framed by fictional publishing-house owners Dan and Barbara Glenn. The frozen GRH container preserves 32 distinct regular-series recordings; the separate Bela Lugosi audition is not present. WGN/Mutual origination and Harry S. Goodman transcription syndication are kept distinct from the frozen long-run numbering.
GRH documents the program through Preserved WGN / Mutual / Goodman transcription span (August 19, 1945 to August 9, 1946) on [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Forrest Lewis (performer on 30 recordings), Nanette Sargent (performer on 30 recordings), and Rye Billsbury (announcer on 30 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.09b709d4bde5c263|Mutual Broadcasting System]] (broadcast on network) and [[org|org.06b4214104618161|WGN]] (originated at station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include mystery and whodunit investigation, publishing, manuscripts and editorial framing, murder and homicide, death, corpses and mortal danger, justice, proof and criminal evidence, and dark humor and comic mystery.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including WGN Chicago mystery anthology, Harry S. Goodman transcription syndication, Publishing-house framing device, and Transcription-disc preservation and numbering.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|cbs-radio-workshop|CBS Radio Workshop]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|escape|Escape]] (1 shared credited people), [[show|have-gun-will-travel|Have Gun, Will Travel]] (1 shared credited people), and [[show|let-george-do-it|Let George Do It]] (1 shared credited people).
